subject: Virtual-ledger mapping & remit instructions for multi-entity invoice flow — BrightLine pilot
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightline.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Remit & invoice flow for Redwood — subsidiary split details

Hi Kimberly / team,

Thanks for walking us through the demo last week. Our AP team dug into the first sample invoice and wants to confirm how remittance and VAT will be represented when we receive split charges across our US entity and our EU subsidiary.

A few concrete asks from AP:
- Can each invoice line point to a "virtual ledger" code that we can map to our GL so our ERP can auto-apply cost centers?
- For EU-sourced services, we need a VAT element on the invoice and a separate VAT identification string for the EU entity.
- Remit instructions: BrightLine prefers a single consolidated PDF for payment but with a per-entity stub (so payments can be split to different bank accounts by our treasury).

I've attached our internal remit worksheet that shows how AP expects to receive the split. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
Director, Finance Operations
BrightLine Health

Attachments: BrightLine-remit-worksheet.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightline.ai>, BrightLine Accounts Payable <ap@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Virtual-ledger mapping & remit instructions for multi-entity invoice flow — BrightLine pilot

Hi Elena — thanks for the worksheet, that's helpful. Quick responses to the asks and next steps: 

1) Virtual ledger codes: yes — we can emit a dedicated metadata column on each invoice line called "virtual_ledger_id" (example values in the attached template). That value is purely informational and can be used by your ERP to route the line to a cost center.

2) VAT handling: we will include a separate VAT block per invoice when applicable. For EU-entity charges we will populate VAT ID and VAT amount per line and a summary VAT line. We will also add the "invoice_entity" tag so the invoice can be programmatically split post-ingest.

3) Consolidated PDF with per-entity stubs: we can produce a combined PDF containing the consolidated charge plus detachable stubs marked with target bank account and account code.

Next steps I propose:
- See the attached "virtual-ledger-template.csv" for the column schema we will populate.
- Marissa / Rishi: can you validate the mapping between our virtual_ledger_id values and BrightLine's GL codes (Marissa: cost center matching; Rishi: tax/VAT tagging)?
- Elena: if that looks good we'll produce a sample pair of invoices for 2026-08 to show the full flow (CSV + PDF + metadata in the API response).

I'll follow up with a short SOW amendment to capture the additional deliverables.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: virtual-ledger-template.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightline.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Virtual-ledger mapping & remit instructions for multi-entity invoice flow — BrightLine pilot

Thanks Kim / Elena — reviewed the template quickly. A couple of practical notes from our side: 

- Cost center mapping: BrightLine's GL has both a 6-digit cost center and a department prefix. I'd like to map virtual_ledger_id -> cost_center (6 digits) + dept prefix column. Suggest we add an optional "dept_prefix" column to the CSV to avoid ambiguity.
- Currency and rounding: when splitting a single invoice amount by entity, we should include a reconciliation line for rounding differences (label it "allocation_adjustment").
- VAT jurisdiction: For EU lines, we need both the VAT percentage and the jurisdiction code (e.g., DE, FR). Populate both in the VAT_jurisdiction column.

I attached a one‑page example (in the Drive link) showing a mock invoice split between US and DE entities with the allocation_adjustment line. Once Rishi confirms the tax tagging, we can test with a sandbox invoice.

Marissa
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightline.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Virtual-ledger mapping & remit instructions for multi-entity invoice flow — BrightLine pilot

Elena / team — confirming tax/VAT approach and next steps. 

- VAT tagging: We'll include VAT_rate, VAT_amount, and VAT_jurisdiction per line. The VAT ID field will be populated when charges are invoiced to the EU entity. For our API output we'll add a top-level metadata object named "tax_breakdown" in the response, and a CSV column "tax_breakdown_json" that contains a compact JSON string (examples in the template) for downstream parsers.
- Remit PDF: We'll attach the consolidated PDF and include per-entity bank details under each stub. BrightLine's preferred remit reference (PO + project code) will be printed on each stub.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: please finalize the short SOW amendment (I saw the draft; add the deliverables: CSV schema + consolidated PDF + one month of test invoices).
- Elena: share the BrightLine GL mapping file (if you can export cost center codes and dept prefixes that will speed mapping).
- Marissa: add "dept_prefix" column to the template and include the sample allocation_adjustment logic.

Once we have the sample invoice pair we'll run it through your ERP ingest flow to validate automatic allocation and bank split.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Manager, Finance Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOW_amendment_v2.pdf (forthcoming), virtual-ledger-template.csv
